lead.kicker: TOP STORY  •  SAUDI ARABIA AND YEMEN
lead.headline: Football and Tennis Moved as Missiles Keep Flying
lead.deck: Saudi Arabia says it stopped a missile aimed at its capital on Thursday.
body: Saudi Arabia is fighting a war with the Houthis, a group in Yemen. Yemen is the country just south of Saudi Arabia. On Wednesday, the Houthis said they hit an Aramco site in Dhahran. Aramco is Saudi Arabia’s giant oil company. A Saudi official said a building was hit and nobody was hurt.

On Thursday, Saudi-backed forces said they stopped a drone heading for the city of Medina and a missile fired toward Riyadh, the capital. Last weekend, attacks on Riyadh’s airport reportedly killed 14 people. It is expected to stay shut until Saturday.

The war is changing daily life. The Saudi football league moved three games. Cristiano Ronaldo’s team, Al Nassr, now plays its match in March 2027. A big tennis event in Riyadh moved to December. In Yemen, government forces began a push to retake land on the coast.

world.headline: Ships Keep Getting Hit Near a Key Oil Waterway
world.deck: Oil costs about $104 a barrel, much more than before the war began.
body: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow sea passage. In February, the United States and Israel attacked Iran, and Iran closed the strait. Before the war, at least one fifth of the world’s oil and gas passed through it.
A June ceasefire fell apart over who controls the strait. The US now blocks Iran’s southern ports. A UK centre counted 15 attacks on ships between October 6 and 14.
When less oil gets out, prices rise. Oil was about $72 a barrel before the war, nearly $120 at its highest, and about $104 on Thursday.
